actor_type.description: Entity type of the actor. Human sessions and character runtimes are distinct types.

attribution_identity.description: Identity attribution set from directive section 4. UNKNOWN is a valid attribution and means the author is not known. Never merge physical humans with rendered or fictional representations.

authority_role.description: Frozen CC-90-001 authority roles. Creator approves canon. AI proposes only.

claim_status.description: Frozen CC-90-001 vocabulary. Seven statuses, no additions during the first 90 days.

consent_record.description: Every consent is a record, not an assumption. Consent is revocable. Revocation is recorded and takes effect for future actions.

consent_type.description: What was consented to. ai_double requires an explicit design decision and a consent model; none exists in v0.1.

granted_by_identity_id.description: Reference to the identity record of the person who consented.

how_given.description: How the consent was given, for example direct statement by the participant, recorded with date and channel.

scope.description: Scope of the consent: what it covers and where it applies.

event_attribution.description: Attribution fields carried by every event in the executed history ledger. With these fields the system can answer what happened, who did it, who witnessed it, when it occurred, which branch it occurred in, what changed, and whether it came from authored history or executed history.

actor_identity.description: Identity value of the actor. UNKNOWN when the actor is not known.

actor_identity_id.description: Reference to the actor identity record, or null when UNKNOWN.

authority.description: Authority under which the event was authorized.

branch.description: Which branch the event occurred in. Every world write names its branch.

consent_record_ids.description: Consent records in effect for the action, by reference. Empty when no consent was required.

history_kind.description: recovered for pre-genesis source material, executed for events that actually occurred after the simulation began. Executed events are always executed.

receipt_hash.description: Hash-chain link for the receipt where the store supports it, or null.

role_binding_id.description: Binding in effect when the event occurred, or null. Null means no binding; the actor acted as themselves.

role_identity.description: Character role inhabited when the event occurred, or null.

source_ids.description: Source records behind the event, by reference. For executed events this is normally empty; the event itself is the record.

transport.description: direct when first-hand, carried when the material arrived by transport. Carried material is labeled carried with author unverified until a receipt establishes it.

new_value.description: Value after the event. May be any JSON value or null.

prior_value.description: Value before the event. May be any JSON value or null.

target.description: What the event acted on, for example an object id or a location id.

witnesses.description: Identities that witnessed the event, each with its own attribution.

identity_record.description: One identity record per participant, human or character. A human participant and a fictional character are different records and are never merged.

character_name.description: Required when identity is fictional_character. Example: Ellie Hawkes, Reg, Sorev, Brakk, Merlin, Mara Venn, the Doctor.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name. For a human this is the person's name; for a character this is the character's name.

entity_type.description: human for a living participant, character for a fictional character runtime.

human_name.description: Required when identity is other_authorized_human. The named authorized human.

id.description: Immutable identity record id, for example id-noah-physical.

identity.description: Attribution value for this identity. For a named fictional character use fictional_character with character_name set. For a named AI system use ai_system with system_name set.

knowledge_scope.description: Bounded knowledge description for a character runtime: what the character is permitted to know. Null for a human participant. A character must be able to say UNKNOWN.

notes.description: Free text notes. Must not contain private family biography or unpublished manuscript text.

privacy_classes.description: Privacy classes that apply to this identity's spaces and information.

simulation_tier.description: Simulation tier for a character runtime. Tier A: high fidelity. Tier B: event-driven. Tier C: schedules and state machines. Null for a human participant.

status.description: Status of this identity record. Disputed roles stay UNKNOWN until Noah.Physical rules.

superseded_by.description: Id of the identity record that superseded this one, or null. Corrections are additive; the old record stays readable.

system_name.description: Required when identity is ai_system. Example: Merlin, Reg, or another named system.

world.description: Fictional frame for a character runtime, for example Memory's Flame / 2397. Null for a human participant.

privacy_class.description: Privacy classes from directive section 13. Space classes and information classes are both listed here; a record names the class that applies to it.

role_binding_record.description: A human explicitly choosing to play or inhabit a fictional character. Requires explicit consent, is recorded, and remains distinguishable in the event ledger. The system must never silently replace a human with a fictional character.

character_identity_id.description: Reference to the fictional character identity record.

character_name.description: Fictional character inhabited, for example Captain Ashley Hawkes.

consent_record_id.description: Consent record for this binding. The binding must not take effect before consent is recorded.

end_time.description: Null while the binding is active.

human_identity.description: Attribution value of the human. Must be a physical human value.

human_identity_id.description: Reference to the human identity record.

revoked_by.description: Identity that revoked the binding, or null.

scope.description: What the binding covers: locations, actions, or scenes. Empty scope is not permitted.

state.description: active, revoked by the human, or expired.

session_record.description: One session record per human entry into the world. A session is a human session, not a character runtime. Entry, presence, exit, and re-entry are recorded here.

consent_record_id.description: Consent record authorizing this avatar rendering.

representation.description: Authorized rendered representation of the human. The avatar is a representation, not the person.

device.description: Device in use, for example VR headset, phone, desktop.

event_ids.description: Executed events this session caused or witnessed, by reference to the executed history ledger.

exit_time.description: Null while the session is present.

identity.description: Attribution value of the human participant. Must be a physical human value, not a fictional character.

identity_id.description: Reference to the identity record of the human participant.

location.description: Where the session is in the world, for example Jupiter Station / Deck Nine.

permissions.description: Permissions granted to this session by Governance and by the Creator.

presence_state.description: present while in the world, exited after leaving, paused if the world is paused for this session.

prior_session_id.description: Previous session record for the same identity, for re-entry linkage. Null on first entry.

privacy_classes.description: Privacy classes applying to this session.

visibility.description: Who may observe this session: private, family, public, or restricted.

role_binding_id.description: Role binding in effect for this session, or null. Default is null: no binding.

description: Multi-user identity model for RRE Genesis v0.1. Draft, November 6, 2026. Covers identity records, session records, role binding records, privacy classes, consent records, and event-ledger attribution fields. No em dashes are used in this schema. Status values follow the frozen CC-90-001 vocabulary where a status field appears. This schema does not promote candidate fiction into canon.
title: RRE Genesis v0.1 Identity Schema
